findings.title: 437 of 465 gateway calls from the apps' BFF routes have no timeout
findings.description: BFF routes call `${GATEWAY}/api/...` with fetch and no AbortSignal. The gateway itself now bounds slow upstreams (NEW-W), but when the gateway is the slow part — the 'Backend Offline' freeze — every pending BFF call waits until Vercel kills the function, and the screen shows a spinner instead of the state screen. The template's own session-refresh (8 s) is one of the 28 that do set one.

evidence.observation: 439/467 calls, every app 1–4 with a signal
gateway-side timeouts exist; app-side do not

findings.root_cause: No shared gateway-fetch helper; each route calls fetch directly.
findings.technical_impact: A slow gateway ties up a function per pending call; failures surface late and as timeouts, not as the 502/504 the screens handle.
findings.business_impact: During an incident users see endless loading instead of "try again".
findings.recommendation: One shared gatewayFetch(path, init) in the template (AbortSignal.timeout, default 10 s) used by every BFF route; template-sync carries it.
acceptance_criteria: No BFF fetch to the gateway without a timeout (a check in CI)
A test: a hung gateway → the route answers 504 within the limit

remediation.note: src/lib/gateway-fetch.ts (shared via template-sync): fetch with a deadline just past the gateway's own 504 (25 s) — 30 s, 90 s for an /ai/ path (the gateway waits 75 s for TEC AI) — so a live gateway always answers first and nothing it would complete is cut (a payment approve included); a caller's own signal still works. 435 gateway calls in 25 repositories (437 matched, the Hub's 2 own-origin calls then restored) moved onto it by a codemod; gateway-fetch.test.ts (shared) checks the deadlines and fails on any bare gateway fetch left in src/, with a self-check that the search finds one. Each repository: tsc, lint and its full suite green. Correction: two of the 467 calls counted in Run 3 were the Hub calling its OWN origin (${req.nextUrl.origin}/api/auth/refresh) — not gateway calls; they are left as they were and the search now exempts own-origin calls. True count: 465 gateway calls, 437 without a deadline.
remediation.verification: After deploy, with the gateway stopped: a BFF route answers with its error within ~30 s instead of hanging

findings.title: The BFFs bypass the server SDK: one file per app imports it, and gateway responses are not schema-validated
findings.description: C-47 §14 says public integration goes through @yasser172/tec-sdk and every response is Zod-validated. In practice each app imports the SDK in a single file (src/lib/sdk.ts; none at all in Assets, Commerce, Life) and makes its 400+ gateway calls with raw fetch, reading the JSON as-is. The SDK itself was last changed on 13 Sep (1.4.0). So the contract the SDK is meant to pin is not the contract the apps use, and a backend shape change reaches the screens unchecked — the class of the nested-envelope Pro-status bug the template already documents.
findings.root_cause: The SDK covers payment/auth; domain routes were written straight against the gateway.
findings.technical_impact: Forbidden #5 (divergent SDK contract vs backend) cannot be detected; responses are trusted unvalidated.
findings.business_impact: A backend change can silently blank a screen or mis-gate a paid feature in many apps at once.
findings.recommendation: Do not wrap 400 calls at once. Decide in an ADR whether domain calls belong in the SDK; meanwhile validate at the edge with the shared gatewayFetch (0033) taking a zod schema for the money and entitlement routes first.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR records where domain contracts live
Payment, wallet and subscription BFF responses are schema-checked

findings.title: The template's example route /api/bff/items calls a gateway path that does not exist
findings.description: Of 712 gateway paths the apps call, 709 match a route in the gateway registry. The other three: two are tests that call the app's own origin, and the third is /api/items, called by the example route src/app/api/bff/items that the template ships and 20 apps still carry. No gateway prefix serves it, so the live route can only fail.
findings.root_cause: A copy-me example kept in production builds.
findings.technical_impact: A public route that always errors; noise in logs and error reports.
findings.business_impact: None to users unless something links to it.
findings.recommendation: Move the example out of src/app (e.g. docs/examples) in the template; remove it from the apps that do not use it.
acceptance_criteria: No app ships /api/bff/items unless the gateway serves /api/items

remediation.note: The example moved to docs/examples/bff-route.example.ts (still type-checked); removed from the 20 apps where it was the unchanged copy and nothing called it; template-sync carries the example and the helper instead.
